questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a traffic signal is ahead. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: A broken white line in the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is allowed when safe.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A broken line means you can pass when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: U-turns are not allowed.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a red slash means an action is prohibited. Do not make U-turns where this sign is posted.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic is coming from both directions ahead.

questions.question: A solid white line in the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yield sign.
questions.explanation: A triangular sign pointing down is always a yield sign. Be ready to slow down or stop.

questions.question: What do five-sided signs mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: School zones.
questions.explanation: Five-sided signs indicate a school zone. Watch for children and pedestrians near schools.

questions.question: Which road is most slippery in cold weather after snow or rain?

options.text: A road in a shaded area

questions.correctAnswerText: A road in a shaded area
questions.explanation: Shaded areas freeze before other parts of the road and thaw after. On cold, wet days, shaded spots become icy.

questions.question: Your license can be suspended if you are under 21 and drive with any blood alcohol level of:
questions.correctAnswerText: Any amount.
questions.explanation: There is zero tolerance for alcohol use by drivers under 21. Any amount of alcohol will result in severe penalties, including a two-year license suspension.

questions.question: When a car with Anti-Lock Brakes loses traction on a slippery road, what should you do?

options.text: Press and hold the brake pedal.
Press and hold the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Press down hard on the brake pedal and hold it. Steer away from danger. The Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) will pump the brakes automatically. Releasing pressure or pumping manually will disable the ABS.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a hill or incline with a curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Turn your front wheels sharply toward the curb.
Turn your front wheels slightly to the right.
Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels sharply away from the curb when parking uphill. This prevents your vehicle from rolling into traffic if the brakes fail. If there is no curb, turn your wheels sharply toward the edge of the road.

questions.question: Blood alcohol content (BAC) depends on each of the following, except:

options.text: How much time passes between drinks.

questions.correctAnswerText: How physically fit you are.
questions.explanation: BAC depends on how much alcohol you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your weight. Physical fitness does not affect BAC. Your ability to "hold your liquor" also does not affect your actual BAC level.

questions.question: If two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The largest vehicle has the right-of-way.
The car on the left has the right-of-way.
The car on the left shall yield to the car on the right.
The car on the right shall yield to the car on the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car on the left shall yield to the car on the right.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. The driver on the left can proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow arrow at a traffic signal, what should you do?

options.text: Should merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.
Should come to a complete stop.
May turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Have the right-of-way and may expect oncoming traffic to stop for them.

questions.correctAnswerText: May turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow means you can turn left in the direction of the arrow. However, you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians first because they have a green light.

questions.question: When you park uphill on a street with a curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Keep the front wheel straight and set the parking brake.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the back wheels into the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels sharply to the left, away from the curb. If your brakes fail, your vehicle will roll toward the curb instead of into traffic.

questions.question: When are streets and highways most slippery?

options.text: When it has been raining hard for several hours.
When they are clean and dry.
Just after it starts to rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just after it starts to rain.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery during the first half hour of rain. Water mixes with oil and other chemicals on the road surface that have not yet washed away. Be extra careful when it first starts raining.

questions.question: When must you pull over to let an emergency vehicle pass?

options.text: Only if it is following you.
Only if it is approaching you from the opposite direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Regardless of your direction.
questions.explanation: You must pull over to the right edge of the road and stop for any emergency vehicle with flashing lights. This applies whether the vehicle is coming from behind you or from the opposite direction.

questions.question: When you approach a railroad crossing without warning signals or gates, what should you do?

options.text: Cross the tracks immediately and as quickly as possible.
Always stop before crossing the tracks.
Prepare to yield to any train at the crossing.
Speed up to beat any oncoming train.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare to yield to any train at the crossing.
questions.explanation: Always be ready to yield to any train at the crossing, especially if there are no lights or gates. Wait until your entire vehicle can fit on the other side of the tracks before crossing. Do not shift gears while crossing because your vehicle might stall.

questions.question: How far away from a fire hydrant is it illegal to park?
questions.correctAnswerText: 10 feet
questions.explanation: It is illegal to park within 10 feet of a fire hydrant.

questions.question: How should you make room for cars entering the freeway?
questions.correctAnswerText: Merge into a different lane.
questions.explanation: Merge into the next lane if possible to create a gap for entering vehicles. If you cannot merge, slow down to let them enter safely. Help them join traffic as smoothly as possible.

questions.question: You should leave extra space when stopping:
questions.correctAnswerText: On a hill.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space in front of your vehicle when stopped on an uphill slope. If the car ahead rolls backward when traffic moves again, you will have room to avoid a collision.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Always stop, even if there is no stop sign.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always honk your horn when you see children.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: This pentagonal sign means you are near a school zone or school crossing. Stay alert and be prepared to stop.

questions.question: When entering the highway on a short entrance ramp with no acceleration lane, you should:

options.text: Immediately enter the right lane and speed up to match traffic.
Use the shoulder to reach traffic speed.
Speed up only after you find a gap in traffic, then enter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up only after you find a gap in traffic, then enter.
questions.explanation: On a short entrance ramp with no acceleration lane, wait for a gap in traffic to appear. Then speed up and enter the highway. You may need to stop while waiting for the right gap.

questions.question: When you see a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line, with the broken line next to you, may you pass?

options.text: Yes, if you are on an expressway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if traffic is clear.
questions.explanation: When there is a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line, and the broken line is on your side, you may cross to pass if no traffic is coming toward you.

questions.question: What color are signs for public recreation areas?
questions.correctAnswerText: Brown.
questions.explanation: Brown signs show cultural, historical, or public recreation areas. They help you find places when traveling in unfamiliar areas.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: All drivers who arrived before you.
The driver on your right, no matter who arrived first.
The driver on your left, no matter who arrived first.
The driver across from you, no matter who arrived first.

questions.correctAnswerText: All drivers who arrived before you.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, the driver who arrives first goes first. If two or more drivers arrive at the same time, the driver on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Continue on the freeway and find another route.
Go to the next exit, leave the freeway, and return to your correct exit.
Back up on the road or shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Back up on the road or shoulder.
questions.explanation: Do not back up on the road or shoulder if you miss your exit. Continue to the next exit or crossroad instead. Other drivers will not expect you to back up, which could cause a crash.

questions.question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, you should:

options.text: Look left and right to see what is coming.
Slowly pass cars that seem to be stopped for no reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left and right to see what is coming.
questions.explanation: At any place where people may cross your path or where traffic lines meet, look to both sides to make sure nothing is coming.

questions.question: When two vehicles enter an intersection at the same time from different roads, which must yield?
questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left
questions.explanation: At any intersection, when two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: Your gas pedal sticks open while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Turn off the ignition without locking the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the ignition without locking the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If your gas pedal sticks, turn off the ignition carefully to avoid locking the steering wheel. Then apply your brakes and move to a safe area off the road.
